desc:
Stretching both west and east, the wide paved Old East Road passes through the
city of Bree. A small patch of grass ends south of the road in a sloping drop
into a small lake. North a door opens into a small timber house. The west gate
of Bree is nearby, while the city of Bree grows eastwards.
name: Old East Road

desc:
From the solid black building to the north a solid timber wall rises tall up in
the air, featuring a wide wooden gate fixed using metal hinges. The gate has a
latch fixed with a chain, to stop just anyone opening the gate from the inside.
The sound of water can be heard from the south just down a slippery grass slope,
and north a black door leads into the gatekeeper's house. A wooden sign is fixed
to the gate.
name: West Gate of Bree

desc:
The passage between the hedge to the west and the tall gate to the east creates
a fourteen yard wide shaded place. The gates are set shallow in a tall timber
wall, both to the south and north the wall bends out and goes into the hedge,
not allowing any passage. Deep tracks in the ground where the gate has been
opened are clearly visible, showing the gate's frequent use.
name: Outside the West Gate of Bree

desc:
Growing massively thick and tall, the hedge marking the western border of Bree
has been cut to allow travellers through. The opening is over ten yards wide,
just like the road travelling straight west and east. The road widens on either
side of the almost ten yard wide hedge, travelling west towards the Shire and
east to Bree.
name: Under a Large Hedge

desc:
A broad and shallow stream slowly moves westward, watering the nearby hedge
before disappearing under the western walls. The crystalline water flows over
jutting rocks, and cream-coloured sand covers the stream's bottom. The Old East
Road heads further into Bree to the north.
name: Slow Creek

desc:
A clear pond sits among grass and reeds bordering the Old East Road. The water
is deep and calm, and the pond's silty floor is ruffled by darting fish, dashing
to safety from onlookers. To the north, the road heads east and west within
Bree.
name: Placid Pond

desc:
A large dock has been built on pilings reaching over the city fishing spot here,
allowing easy access with boat or a fishing rod. On the dock a solid shack has
been built, with thick walls facing west and east while open both north and
south. Inside, tools for the fishing trade are being kept while a fireplace and
a few chairs provide heat and comfort. Clear water laps against the sides of the
dock.
name: Pier upon a Small Pond

desc:
The stone road comes to a wider stretch here, and is now a mixture of smaller
stones among the large stone blocks. A few blocks seems loose on the northern
side, where water seems to have washed away some of the dirt. Just off the road
to the north a large dock sticks out over the water. To the south a triangular
wall dominates the view and not far west the road comes to and end.
name: Mason Road

desc:
The large stone blocks come to an abrupt end where the road widens into a dirt
packed square. Westwards rises a steep hill where a large green hedge stretches
towards the skies. A small cemetery can be seen over a stone fence, and can be
accessed though a wooden gate.
name: End of Mason Road

desc:
The road here is built from packed red clay. Wheel tracks have created two ruts
in the dirt making the footing uneven. The walls of the houses bordering the
street are mostly covered in a deep red moss, giving the whole area a desert
feel.
name: Southwind Lane

desc:
A high wooden fence surrounds a few of the houses here. The foot of the fence is
caked with dirt from the road and little bits of greenery can be seen growing on
it. The street consists of packed, reddish-brown clay with sprigs of grass
poking up all along it.
name: Southwind Lane

desc:
Large patches of ivy grow along the sides of the narrow lane. The walls of the
houses bordering the street have long strings of ivy crawling up them. Some
wooden planks have been placed on the ground here and there acting as a solid
place to stand if the road turns to mud.
name: Southwind Lane

desc:
Well-maintained grass stretches about the plaza around a wide stone dais raised
in the centre. The masonry of the dais seems to be fairly rudimentary with many
of the stone blocks being of slightly varying dimensions. Houses surrond the
plaza to the north, west, and south.
name: Highbluff Plaza

desc:
The few patches of grass still visible here are struggling with their survival
clearly being stepped on and kicked often. Timber and wooden structures make up
several training apparatus for the guards and others using this room for their
battle readiness. Some are made to climb, others to go under and they seem to be
placed in a circle so one could change the training during an exercise. A few
large timber man-like figures have deep wounds from swords, spears and axes
being slammed into them. A sign reading 'Quartermaster and Warrior Trainer' is
pointing west. North, a stone building housing the guards rises and eastwards
the path leading into Bree can be seen.
name: Training Grounds

desc:
Almost being a part of the training grounds, it still somehow manages to be
barred from most sounds. Two solid and tall timber walls with a tarped roof
being slanted using timber crossbeams allows some cover from both wind and
precipitation. A large number of weapons and armour resembling the ones used by
the Bree guards can be seen on display, covering most of the two walls.
name: Quartermaster's Corner

desc:
This portion of Westhill Way is a little worse for wear, evidenced mostly by a
large, muddy pothole that mars one side of the road. A small pool of brown water
lies in the bottom of the hole, and the grass beside the road has begun to
develop deep ruts from wagons forced to detour around the damage.
name: Westhill Way

desc:
Westhill Way turns here, leading into the heart of Westhill to the north and
back toward Bree proper to the east. A few houses cover the hillside, most of
which have carefully trimmed shrubbery lining the footpaths that lead to each
front door.
name: Westhill Way

desc:
This corner of Westhill Way marks the end of the main throughfare of the south
side of Westhill. A few larger homes have been constructed in the hills here,
with tall, multi-paned windows displaying a bit of extravagance amid the
otherwise utiliarian achitecture that marks much of Bree.
name: Westhill Way

desc:
Here, the wide road of Westhill Way joins with the more narrow North Ridge
Avenue. Large houses sit on each corner, with well-manicured, grassy lawns. Each
has a well-cut wooden fence marking the edge of each yard.
name: Junction of Westhill Way and North Ridge Avenue

desc:
The manicured stone ground is free from imperfections and bumps, and provides a
safe ground for practicing by the warrior guild members. Tall stone walls
provide cover from wind, and a drain in the yard centre provides a spot for rain
water to collect.
name: Training Yard

desc:
A damp floor of packed dirt holds several cots and bunk beds, with grass packed
mattresses for sleeping. The walls and roof seem solid, made out of different
wood, timber and a few stones - clearly built from leftovers. A few torches
throw a dim but dancing light, and a fireplace near the entrance warms anyone
living here.
name: Poor House

desc:
Beneath a steep hill both to the west and south, memorial plaques and stones
have been placed, shaded by the Bree hedge growing above. Pathways of white
gravel marbled with grey and black pass though the well tended grassy area. In
several places, flowers and lights have been put down in someone's memory.
name: Well-tended City Cemetery

desc:
Both northern and southern walls are triangular, meeting at a high peak almost
twenty feet up. All walls have been coloured green to about a man's height and
white to the top. Two massive chandeliers are suspended from the ceiling, with
large white candles lighting the room and two solid iron candelabrums on each
side of a large desk.
name: Seer's Lodging

desc:
This house is built with a timber front, clad in large slabs of wood painted
brightly green on both the inside and outside. Towards the back the house is dug
deep into a hillside, with solid clay covered walls and ceiling. A small kitchen
and a stone clad fireplace cover most of the eastern wall.
name: A Small House

desc:
Built just inside the Bree west gate, this house stands tall and wide. The roof
slopes only northwards, making an impressively tall front towards the Old East
Road. Tall black planks cover the outside, while the insides are painted in a
pale yellow colour.
name: Harry's Manor

desc:
Built from a foundation of solid stone five feet high and continuing into a
timber frame this tower stands high. Through a tall arched opening eastwards a
large garden can be seen downhill, and on the eastern wall a solid winding
staircase rises twenty feet up towards a platform.
name: Sorcerer's Stone Tower

desc:
A platform is formed from the inside of the tower, stretching close to the Bree
hedge to the west. The balcony is solidly framed with a railing, walls and a
roof stretching overhead. A few hanging potted plants frame the view west, where
the intersection between the Old East Road and the Greenway can be seen.
name: Shielded Balcony

desc:
Only one extra wall is built to house the teaching grounds of Bree. Being set in
a corner with the Bree barracks and jail both east and north, large stone walls
enclose this yard on three sides. The western wall is not nearly as tall as the
other two, only being about six feet. Beyond the western wall the taller green
hedge of Bree can be easily seen, quite a few branches even climb into this
yard.
name: Practice Yard

desc:
Built from stacked stones and isolated with large sacks of packed dirt, this
room dampens the noise from the busy training grounds outside. A large number of
chairs surround two large tables, allowing the Bree city guards a retreat from
the daily rotation. A kitchen with utensils and cups is placed along the eastern
wall, with a large basin of water for cleaning easily available for cleaning.
Through an opening in the stone wall north, an office can be spotted and
southwards through an oblique opening the training grounds can be reached.
name: City Barracks

desc:
The centrepiece of this office is a large desk, made from an elaborate timber
structure. It spans over twelve feet and could easily fit several but only one
man sits at the desk. All visitors are pointed to the bench along the eastern
wall, under a large shelf holding several leather bound books. Several weapons
confiscated from criminals are stacked in a corner, under constant watch from
the guards. The office opens southwards through a stone opening into the guards'
barracks, and a heavy iron gate bars the way into the prison west.
name: Chief of Bree's Office

desc:
A comfortable-looking tavern stands at the edge of the park. It has been built
with a respect to its surroundings, embracing the peaceful and calm athmosphere
of the park. Flowers and herbs grow around the tavern while big, old trees
stretch upwards warding this serene place. A warm light glints from the inn's
round windows, welcoming everyone to drop by.
name: In Front of the Riding Maiden's Inn

desc:
This wide, cosy tavern belongs to Temperance and is rumoured to serve the best
beer in Bree! The brown- and gold-themed room is covered with broad floor planks
and filled with oaken tables which come in two heights; customized to fit the
needs of the big and little folk of Bree. The far end of the room is dominated
by a long, smooth bar behind which stands a tall shelf, filled with bottles of
all sorts and a healthy assortment of pipe weed. A few paintings, a roaring
fireplace in the corner and the yellow thatched roof above complete the Inn's
interior decoration.
name: The Riding Maiden's Inn

desc:
The distinctive rough red brick laid into the ground here spearates North Ridge
Avenue from the old cobblestones of Westhill Way to the south. A few houses,
also built from the same red brick, top the mounds of the hills lining the
street.
name: North Ridge Avenue

desc:
The street here is composed of a reddish dirt similar to clay. Wheel tracks are
carved into the road by the countless wagons and carts that have crossed this
path. The road here branches off to the east, west, and south, making this a
fairly busy intersection.
name: Westhill Way

desc:
Low wooden fences surround the houses bordering the road. Large trees tower
above the fences, curling over the street. The road here is lined with small
pebbles, apparently an attempt by the local residents to improve the look of the
ageing streets.
name: Westhill Way

desc:
Here, Bluff Street and Westhill Way come to a crossing. The ground surrounding
cobblestones streets is mostly dirt, with a few muddy spots. At the centre of
the crossroads, a tall, iron, lampost stands like a beacon welcoming all who may
come to this convergence.
name: Intersection of Bluff Street and Westhill Way

desc:
The street narrows here, almost like an alley that has been squeezed between
houses. Snaking vines climb up the walls of the houses in their relentless
pursuit of the sun. The walls of the houses, primarily made of stone, have been
cracked from the tight embrace of the vines.
name: Side Street

desc:
The alley comes to an abrupt stop here. Tall houses constructed of mud-like
bricks surround the street. The road itself used to be cobblestone but has been
worn down to the point where it is now equal parts mud and pebbles.
name: End of a Small Alley

desc:
A low stone wall, crumbling and borken, wraps around some patchy lawns in front
of the houses here. Covered in dead vines, the houses are built with shoddy laid
stonework. The sloping roofs above are weather torn and appear to be barely
holding on.
name: Bluff Street

desc:
The ground is strewn with a white-grey gravel that crunches underfoot. In one
corner of the square, some holes have been dug into the ground where a wide
hitching post stands a few feet above the ground. The footprints of horses
litter the ground.
name: Western Square

desc:
A neat row of grey stones lays along the sides of this pebble strewn road. The
disparately sized pebbles are covered in mud and clay. A row of small, thorny,
bushes lines the street on either side, making it perilous to crowd too closely
in the road.
name: Bluff Street

desc:
The grass stops abruptly and turns into mud as it approaches the pond. The water
itself is relatively clear, though the muddy surface beneath gives it a brown
tint. A shoddy wooden pier juts out into the water almost reaching the centre of
the pond.
name: Small Pond

desc:
You descend a set of stairs from the entrance into a great white tunnel. Its
walls are covered in tapestries and paintings of ancient realms. The stairs are
made of marble and onyx. At the base of the stairs there is a tall portal of
polished metal with intricate designs inlaid with gems and runes. Beyond the
passage is another even greater chamber that seems to have a strange aura
emanating from it.
name: Arched Tunnel

desc:
Only about four feet in height and width near the entrance from above, growing
larger towards the eastern end this stone crypt holds shelves on any available
surface. They are filled with small vials, flasks and trinkets, most of these
covered with a thick layer of dust.
name: Dimly Lit Stone Crypt

desc:
A hushed tone pervades this cramped hall under the eaves of southern Bree's
foundation. The low room has stone-laid recesses set into the walls. In these
lie the decayed remains of the ancient Edain of many millennia ago. Ancient
writings in a dialect of Westron describe the occupants, but the precise
meanings cannot be gleaned, so changed is the modern language from its forebear.
name: Quiet Resting Place

desc:
Hardly any sunlight is being admitted into this small and dank room. The windows
on the southern side have been draped with heavy curtains, disallowing the
passer-by from Highbluff Plaza even a glimpse from the interior. The wooden
walls have been decorated with numerous paintings of coins, jewellery, weapons
and artefacts.
name: Scylhiun's Shelter

desc:
As you pass the threshold into this chamber you notice the floor is laid out
before you in dark green marble as if it was a field of grass, and the ceiling
is a black onyx with softly glowing diamonds as if they were stars. Upon the
northern wall is a great throne made of gold and laced with silver. An elegant
marble chest sits against the wall.
name: Inside a Large Throne Room

desc:
You pass behind the throne and enter this final room. Its walls are made of
carved panels of grey wood and the floor is covered in soft green velvet. A
large desk is against the western wall covered in papers and maps. There is a
large painting of Brogan adorning the northern wall. His large bed rests against
the eastern wall, a crown of silver lays on the pillow.
name: Brogan's Quarters

desc:
Atop the roof you enter a small temple dedicated to the Seven Fathers of the
dwarves. A reflecting pool fills the centre of the room and murals cover the
walls depecting the creation of the Dwarves by Aule.
name: Temple of Seven Fathers

desc:
The bedroom is small but cosy, with a single bed placed against the far wall. A
wooden nightstand sits next to the bed, and a small dresser can be found against
another wall. A simple desk sits near a window that overlooks the town of Bree.
The room is decorated with the trappings of a half-elf cleric, with several holy
symbols adorning the walls and a set of prayer beads hanging from the bedpost. A
thick rug covers the floor, adding a touch of warmth and comfort to the space.
Overall, the room is modest but well-kept, reflecting the orderly and
disciplined lifestyle of Melchor.
name: Melchor's Bedroom

desc:
This is a cosy and friendly-looking dwarven home. The walls are covered with
artefacts of different origin: Dwarven, Elven and even some items of Orkish
origin can be found. A low archway, beaming warm light, leads to a bigger room
due west.
name: Entrance Hall

desc:
This room is quite big compared to the others in this home. Not as richly
decorated as the entrance hall, only two notable items are here. A huge
fireplace giving warmth and light can be seen in the corner. And next to it, a
big round table covered with Numenorean carvings. In the southwwest corner are
some stairs leading up the bedroom.
name: Living Room

desc:
This room is rather large. The walls are upholstered with soft, padded leather
plates. There are no windows here and several torches have been set on the walls
to fight the prevailing darkness. Other than that, the room is empty except for
a big weapons rack in the rear of the room.
name: The Training Room

desc:
The most prominent thing in the room is a set of large shelves placed high
against the back wall. On the top shelf there appears to be a million different
pots of spices and herbs useful for seasoning a variety of different foods. On
the lower shelves there are huge pots and pans, the type that would make any
cook jealous. Near the window there is a table large enough for two.
name: The Kitchen

desc:
The bedroom is small, fitting a bed, a table and a big bookshelf. The bed is
neatly done and hasn't been used for some time it seems. A pile of books and
scrolls is on the table, and a lantern giving some light. On the walls you see
items of orcs Chazan has slain over the years: weapons, shields, scalps and a
crude orkish horn.
name: Chazan's Sleeping Quarters

desc:
The balcony is decorated with various kinds of flowers. You can see the tree
tops of Bree's park, leaves shifting and moving in the wind. On the floor of the
balcony you notice a soft, fuzzy rug and a rocking chair is set in one corner.
name: A Small Balcony

desc:
The boulder-strewn hilltops' surface is pocked with moss-filled nooks and
crannies. Within the cracks of the boulders, small colonies of lichens thrive.
The boulders form what appears to be a crude circle, suggestive of an ancient
meeting place. Stonecrop clings stubbornly to the rocky outcrops, their yellow
blossoms adding a dash of colour to the otherwise grey tableau. The west is
marked by a range of hills that roll across the horizon. To the north, a
solitary hillock rises, emerald green and studded with grey stones.
name: Boulder-covered Hilltops

desc:
Along the path, the traveller's gaze is drawn to the fir trees, few but fair,
their verdant spires standing tall against the pastel panorama. Limestone
outcrops, ancient bones of the earth, jut forth from the hillsides. To the west
and east, the hills rise sharply, their steep sides veiled with a mixture of
moss and creeping ivy, a vibrant green tapestry. The trail narrows as it enters
a meandering maze of rolling emerald hills to the north. To the south, the trail
continues into a shallow valley.
name: Winding Trail through the Hillocks

desc:
A turning trail cuts through the verdant canvas, winding its way across the
undulating South Downs landscape. Next to this trail, a huddle of wild marjoram
makes its home, rooted in the heart of a limestone crevice. The trail pushes
onward, its path set to the west and north, further into the heart of the hills.
To the east and south, the hills rise sharply. Their slopes are steep and
treacherous, a deterrent to all but the hardiest of adventurers.
name: Turning Trail across the Hills

desc:
This path, narrow yet steadfast, boasts a worn, weather-beaten surface. It lies
upon a bed of solid rock, etched out from the stony bluff. To the west, the land
rises with daunting, near-vertical sculptures of rock and scrub, far too steep
for any wanderer to traverse. To the east, the trail continues, turning,
twisting, and teetering across the hills. Southward, the trail beckons,
extending its reach toward the open fields beyond the Downs.
name: Trail through the Hillocks

desc:
An overgrown ridge, a forgotten scar of earth and stone, carves its way through
the grassland. Lichen and moss creep across its surface, a green and grey shroud
that softens its starkness. Staghorn clubmoss and reindeer lichen, common in
these boreal climes, claim dominion here, their forms creating a miniature
forest upon the ridge.
name: Overgrown Ridge

desc:
The ground is a patchwork of loose boulders and rocks. A brook babbles its way
through, its clear waters rushing over pebbles and rocks. A solitary hawthorn
tree stands guard near the brook. To the west, the land rises in rocky hilltops,
their jagged edges etch the horizon, forming a rugged skyline. To the east,
hilltops crouch under the weight of boulders. To the north, the land weaves a
junction of hilltops, where the hilltops meet in a convocation of stone and
earth.
name: Centre of a Stretch of Hills

desc:
Dwarf willows and juniper shrubs cling to the crevices and crannies of this
rocky terrain, their roots delving into the stone, finding purchase in the most
unlikely places. A cluster of hillside daisies emerges from a crevice, their
delicate blooms creating a vibrant contrast amidst the monochromatic
surroundings. Amidst the boulders, a solitary Scots pine stands, with a massive
gnarled trunk and twisted branches.
name: Rocky Hilltops

desc:
This plateau is an unattainable expanse, its surface a rugged tapestry of
exposed rock and sporadic vegetation. Boulders, large and ominous, litter the
surface, their surfaces are worn and weathered from countless years of exposure.
Jutting crags of granite and basalt rise like jagged teeth from the plateau,
their stark forms casting long shadows down the slopes.
name: Plateau among the Hills

desc:
Far removed from the Greenway, the trail here is hard to make out from the grass
and short brush. The path moves in a long arc between the west and north. The
area is a meadow sandwiched between two strands of hills of the South Downs.
name: Faint Trail

desc:
The hills of the South Downs have broken away to the northeast and southwest to
reveal a protected prairie. Only slight undulations disrupt an otherwise smooth
area of land. Some burrows are tucked away against the sheltered edges of hills
to the north. Imprints of larger animals indicate a favored route of wild
creatures.
name: Peaceful Field

desc:
A large portion of the ground shows evidence of having been plowed in the past
but never followed through on planting. A small, dilapidated shack nearby
indicates that this was once meant to be farmland but has been abandoned. The
shack only has one wall standing with a jumble of half-burnt wood making up the
rest of the debris.
name: Plowed Field

desc:
This section of the South Downs are a mix of grass-covered hills with large
patches of gravel and pebbles. The portions of the trail traversing the small
rocks show deep hoof marks where previous travellers struggled. The hills
continue to the southeast and northwest.
name: Gravelly Trail

desc:
The ground here is a rugged tapestry, a mosaic of boulders and stones that cover
the little topsoil that remains. Large flat slabs of rock, remnants of some
ancient upheaval, lie strewn haphazardly about the slopes. A rocky outcrop, like
a skeletal hand reaching out from the earth, interrupts the gentle incline to
the west. To the east and north, the land rises sharply, forming steep, imposing
barriers that preclude any passage. A solitary trail, a sinewy ribbon of earth,
can be seen snaking its way in the south.
name: Depression among the Hills

desc:
The hills from the northwest climb higher here and stand on a precipice above
grasslands to the west and south. The ground is a mix of grass and pebbly soil.
A lone tree, long dead, stands on the edge of the cliff to the west. The bark
has been stripped and weathered, a grey trunk with broken limbs is all that
remains.
name: Hilly Overlook

desc:
These hills form the eastern part of a long section of the South Downs extending
to the northwest and the southeast. The mounds rise to the west until they end
in a cliff. The elevation slowly decreases into a field to the north but is
blocked to the east by a jumble of rocks. The large stones appear to have been
pushed upward out of the ground and tumbled back on top of themselves.
name: Patch of Knolls

desc:
The tall hills here follow a winding cliff to the east until smoothing out at a
lower elevation into a large field to the south. Eastern movement is blocked by
a natural wall made of large stones too difficult to climb over. The hills are
covered with dense, short grass.
name: Winding Cliff

desc:
Hills to the north slowly lower down into this stretch of flat ground. Grass and
weeds grow in varying heights creating a scraggly landscape. Thin stalks of
brown vegetation sprout up between patches of grass and dip their heads in lazy
arcs. The fields sprawl out to the west and south with some knolls farther in
the distance.
name: Wild Field

desc:
The elevation of the grassy plains here seems to be slightly lower than the
surrounding fields causing water to slowly collect. The result is a lush meadow
where each imprint in the ground sends mud squishing out of the roots of the
grass.
name: Muddy Field

desc:
Thick grass grows tall and droops back toward the ground. The vegetation covers
the area completely and appears more pale than the adjoining meadow. The lush
green colour is replaced with something closer to white and appears almost
sickly. A large growth of brush extends to the south.
name: Pale Field

desc:
This hill is clearly part of the South Downs extending to the northwest and
southeast, but is separated by steep edges to the west and east. Exposed rocks
and dirt tumble precipitously from the top of the hill. A patch of brush extends
to the north.
name: Isolated Mound

desc:
The area is covered in knee-high bushes. They are remarkably stiff and make
movement difficult as the branches tug and resist shifting. The ground between
bushes is sparse grass mixed with broken twigs and dirt. Some large boulders
partially obscure a cave in the hill to the west.
name: Short Brush

desc:
Some worn bones have been collected into a corner of this cave. It appears to
have been used by a bear or other wild animals at some point but has since seen
further excavation to expand the area shown by a stark contrast in wall textures
as the cave moves deeper into the hill. Tin and iron cooking equipment is
scattered around a fire pit with animal furs in a pile nearby.
name: Abandoned Bear Den

desc:
Through the dense, creeping plants covering the ground, there is faint evidence
of a path that runs north to south. The path has not been maintained or used
regularly, and as a result, plants have overgrown it, making it difficult to see
and use. It is unclear where the path leads, but it is a reminder of a time when
this area was more heavily travelled.
name: Overgrown Path

desc:
The centre of the area was once a crossroads where paths trail off to the north
and south. Fainter tracks split off to the west and east but it isn't clear if
they were created by animals or human inhabitants. Bushes and creeping vines
have enveloped the landscape.
name: Overgrown Crossing

desc:
A long abandoned trail snakes between the north and south. Grass covering the
hills to the south covers the trail as it climbs in that direction. Dense vines
prevent grass from growing over the old path as it moves to the north. Leafy
climbing plants resist any movement.
name: Faint Path in the Brush

desc:
A wide field of rough grass covers the area. Wildflowers dot the land adding
shades of colour to the sea of green. A difficult incline begins to the west.
Thick vines interlocking with each other in an impassable mess mark the
beginning of rough brush to the east and south.
name: Secluded Field

desc:
The only gentle slope on the hill is towards the east. All other directions are
precipitously steep. The top of the hill is craggy with rocks of many sizes
strewn unevenly. A few small burrows emerge from the dusty ground near the base
of larger boulders that give cover for small rodents.
name: Steep Hill

desc:
The soft grass is interrupted by a variety of dirt trails intersecting in the
middle of the area. Well-trod paths wind off in all directions except to the
south as a tall hill blocks the way. Animals travelling from grass fields
surrounding the South Downs seem to make regular use of this intersection.
name: Trails in a Field

desc:
Grass of varying length spreads over the area. Some areas are very short, having
been nibbled down nearly to the dirt by the roving animals. Other sections are
frequented less and allowed the vegetation to grow higher. Many hoof prints are
stamped into the ground. A wagon track leads east to a barn.
name: Peaceful Pasture

desc:
Wild flowers of blues, reds, and whites dot the grassland. Perhaps the cliff in
the west provides the perfect amount of daily shade to spur the unusually large
number of blooms. Grass fills in every space where the flowers are not growing.
A valley curves between hills to the north and the field opens up substantially
in the east and south.
name: Flowering Meadow

desc:
The fertile field bends west to south as it bumps against the South Downs to the
north and east. While the valley continues to curve towards the northwest, a
larger field opens up to the south. An unusually high hill for the South Downs
is visible far off to the south, rising above the other mounds.
name: Winding Valley

desc:
This is a very large barn with numerous stalls for animals, hay, and grain
storage. One stall holds barrels of wine while others are reserved for
livestock. Some equipment stands in the corner for processing grapes before
being barrelled. The farm house stands to the east while vineyards and pasture
flow to the south and west.
name: Large Barn

desc:
The sprawling fields of crops are dominated by wheat, with smaller areas of
corn, hay, and oats. Fertile ground has contributed to impressive crop heights.
A garden has been carved out of the field to serve the farm workers. An ageing,
wooden fence encloses the area to the west and south.
name: Wheat Fields

desc:
Long rows of grapevines stretch out north to south. The vines are pruned and
well-kept. Thick brown stalks snake horizontally above the ground with smaller
green vines growing up and over a rope. Billowy green leaves mingle with heavy
bunches of grapes. Soft, short grass covers the fertile soil between rows. A
fence protects the space to the east and south.
name: Vibrant Vineyard

desc:
The inside of the farmhouse is spacious. The front door opens to a crackling
fire warming the living room. To the left is a long hallway with several living
quarters for farmhands. To the right is a bright kitchen filled with ripe
vegetables from the garden and freshly-baked bread.
name: Expansive Farmhouse

desc:
This section of the South Downs becomes fairly narrow between a cliff to the
southwest and thick brush to the east. Some brush from the east has encroached
on ths hill with some thorny vines mingling in the thick grass. The hills
continue along the cliff edge to the west and south.
name: Curving Hill

desc:
A grassy field stretches out, mostly flat but dotted with small holes.
Travellers should be careful not to twist an ankle in one of these holes, as
they are all exposed dirt and have not yet been filled with vegetation. To the
north, a tall hill blocks passage, while impenetrable brush blocks the east.
name: Pitted Field

desc:
The entire area is filled with bushes of varying heights and widths. Some bushes
hug the ground with vines curling out like stiff fingers. Other plants are as
large as a horse with thorny vines growing in tangled messes. While paths can be
made through most of the area, the brush is too dense to the east, north and
south.
name: Thorny Dead End

desc:
The hills of the South Downs reach a high point before the precipitous drop off
of the long cliff. Fields stretch out for many miles below the cliff to the
west. From this height, brush can be seen encroaching on the hills as they
continue to the southeast.
name: High Overlook

desc:
Soft, rolling hills of the South Downs continue here from the west into the
south and east. A large patch of brush encroaches from the north and forms an
impenetrable barrier, blocking movement in that direction. The grass here
appears healthy from fertile soil and plentiful moisture.
name: South Downs

desc:
Tall, leafy plants from the north have begun invading the grassy hills in the
area. The South Downs extend to the west and south. Some established animal
paths coming from the north have beaten down the grass in narrow slits winding
through the hills.
name: South Downs

desc:
The area is lower than the surrounding land. A few tall trees have broken out of
the multitude of bushes and vines tangling the ground. Back to the east is the
only way out of the area as the other directions are too steep and overgrown
with vegetation to traverse.
name: Tangled Dell

desc:
The South Downs hills are smooth and grassy, dominating the landscape. Scattered
trees dot the area, but none grow close enough to form a grove. To the west, a
deep trench prevents movement. The trench is filled with dirt and a few decaying
sticks.
name: South Downs

desc:
The hills of the South Downs slope down to the south into an area full of wild
plants and vegetation. A sharp cliff is to the west and a wide chasm prevents
movement to the east. The sharp trough between hills is unusual in the soft,
rolling hills of the South Downs. It is too wide to leap across and at least
thirty feet deep.
name: South Downs

desc:
The field is overrun by thick flowery brambles, towering overgrown grass, and
patches of lichen that cling to every surface. Shrubs of blackberries grow
around the thickets. The brambles intertwine with one another, creating a
natural barrier that no man could penetrate without great effort.
name: Thick Flowery Brambles

desc:
The thickets seem to form an impenetrable wall, daring any who might venture to
pass through their thorny barrier. Even the bravest of souls might find
themselves lost within the maze of brush, their progress slowed to a crawl by
the tangled web before them. The thorny thickets seem to come alive, writhing
and reaching out, trying to grasp at any who passed by. Amidst the tangled maze,
a small walkway emerges, crossing over a gushing stream. The pathway is narrow,
and made of rough-hewn stones, barely visible among the lush growth.
name: Old Thickets

desc:
The area is largely covered by soft grass. Small, willowy bushes spot the
landscape providing ample area to move around them. A larger patch of bushes
crowd next to the cliff of the South Downs to the east. Stiff bushes crowd in an
impossible wall to the south.
name: Field of Small Bushes
